milestone.title: Agent automation config: commit/push/branch/auto-remediate knobs in project config

intent.outcome: Project config gains an [agent.automation] section with four knobs: commit_after_execute (bool), push_after_review (bool), branch_strategy (per-milestone | current | none), and auto_remediate (none | low | medium | high | all — threshold semantics: remediate findings at or above the level). Agents read these knobs at handoff boundaries (after execute, after self-review, after external review) and branch their behavior: commit the work, push on review handoff, cut a per-milestone branch, and auto-remediate findings at/above the configured threshold or merely record them. raul surfaces the knobs via the M140 config TUI.

problem.description: Today every agent handoff is ad-hoc: the runner commits (or doesn't) based on session judgment, the coordinator pushes (or doesn't) at the review boundary, branch strategy is implicit, and finding remediation is all-or-nothing. There is no shared, project-level policy — so the same project behaves differently across sessions and agents, and the human cannot declare 'always push at review handoff' or 'auto-fix only high-severity findings' once and have every agent honor it.

in_scope: Config model: new [agent.automation] section in config.toml (mp-model config.rs) with fields: commit_after_execute: bool (default false), push_after_review: bool (default false), branch_strategy: enum { per-milestone, current, none } (default current), auto_remediate: enum { none, low, medium, high, all } (default none).

auto_remediate threshold semantics: the value names the MINIMUM severity to remediate. none = record only; low = all severities; medium = medium+high; high = high only; all = alias for low (every severity). Document the ordering none < low < medium < high so 'all' is redundant-with-low but kept for clarity.
mp config set/show: read/write the new section. mp config validate accepts the new fields and their enum values.
raul: the new section appears in the M140 Settings TUI as an [agent.automation] group, editable like other sections.

Agent contract (skills): mp-runner and mp-coordinator updated to read config at handoff boundaries and branch on the knobs — commit after execute if commit_after_execute, push at review handoff if push_after_review, honor branch_strategy, and auto-remediate findings at/above the auto_remediate threshold (else just record them via mp reviews finding).

mp reviews finding: when auto_remediate is set and findings are below threshold, they are recorded but not acted on; at/above threshold, the runner remediation loop engages. The threshold filter is applied by the agent reading config, not by mp gating the command.
out_of_scope: No new mp subcommand for git automation. The agent runs git directly per the config knobs; mp does not wrap git commit/push/branch into its own command surface (mp git status/commit/push exist separately and are unaffected).
No CI/CD pipeline integration. Branch and push are local git operations; continuous integration is downstream and out of scope.
No per-milestone override of the automation config. The knobs are project-level policy. Per-milestone overrides are a later candidate if the need surfaces.
No automatic PR creation. push_after_review pushes to the configured remote; opening a PR remains a manual/harness step.
Does not change the lifecycle state machine or review model — only adds config that agents consult at existing transitions.

design_decisions.choice: auto_remediate names a minimum severity (threshold from the top), not an exclusive set
design_decisions.rationale: A threshold reads naturally ('medium' = med+high) and avoids combinatorial list values. 'all' aliases 'low' (everything) for clarity, accepting the redundancy.

design_decisions.choice: Knobs live in project config.toml under [agent.automation], not in plan.toml or per-user settings
design_decisions.rationale: This is project-level workflow policy a team should share via the repo. config.toml is already mp-managed and sits in the plan-adjacent zone — keeps it out of the hand-edit plan zone while remaining version-controlled.

design_decisions.choice: The agent reads config and branches on it; mp does not gate commands on the knobs
design_decisions.rationale: The knobs describe desired agent behavior at handoff boundaries, not hard CLI gates. mp provides the source of truth; the skills encode the consult-and-act discipline. This avoids coupling git/review commands to config-checking logic.

M140 provides the raul editor surface for the new fields. Adding the fields before the TUI exists means raul cannot manage them; adding after lets the new section get a first-class editing home immediately.

design_decisions.choice: [agent.automation] lives in ProjectConfig at crates/mp/src/config.rs, NOT mp-model config.rs as the original spec body stated
design_decisions.rationale: mp-model/src/config.rs holds only domain types (Decisions/Brief/Ideas). ProjectConfig — the on-disk config.toml schema with Option<T> + unwrap_or accessors — lives in crates/mp/src/config.rs. Same correction applied to M149 S1. Keeps agent.* sections together (M149 agent.runner/coordinator, M147 agent.automation).

design_decisions.choice: auto_remediate names the MINIMUM severity to remediate (at-or-above); none<low<medium<high; all is an alias for low
design_decisions.rationale: An at-or-above threshold matches operator intuition ('fix everything medium and up'). low vs all overlap is deliberate clarity, not redundancy — 'all' reads better in configs that want every severity.

design_decisions.choice: the threshold filter is applied by the agent reading config, not by mp gating mp reviews finding
design_decisions.rationale: mp reviews finding records any severity unconditionally (audit trail must be complete). The decision to ACT is policy, read by the agent at the handoff boundary. Keeps mp a recorder, not a gate, over review severity.

design_decisions.choice: knobs are project-level only; no per-milestone override
design_decisions.rationale: Policy consistency across sessions/agents is the whole point. Per-milestone overrides fragment behavior and defeat the 'declare once' value; defer unless a concrete need surfaces.

findings.description: templates/defaults/config.session.json missing agent.automation block (independent code review finding M147-MEDIUM-1). Fixed by adding the same four-key block to config.session.json
findings.rationale: Session profile users saw null for the four knobs while full/hybrid users saw explicit defaults — UX consistency across profiles. Verified after fix: mp init --profile session now writes agent.automation block.

findings.description: LOW-1 from code review: only 'high' severity was exercised for the explicit 'none' threshold and unset threshold. Extended auto_remediate_threshold_unknown_threshold_treated_as_record_only to cover all three severities (low, medium, high) for both 'bogus' and explicit-'none' paths plus the rank-equality assertion.
findings.rationale: Defensive coverage for the auto_remediate="none" vs unset parity claim. Headline test passed with 9/9 green after fix; rank-equality assertion added to catch a future regression where the sentinel and the string diverge.

findings.description: templates/skills/mp-coordinator/reviewing.md:55 instructs external reviewers to file blocker|major|minor|nit severities, and templates/skills/mp-flow/SKILL.md:145 orders blocker/major first, but crates/mp/src/config.rs:119-130 SeverityRank recognizes only low|medium|high (plus config alias all) and maps every other value to None. An agent following the installed review skill will therefore mark all of its findings record-only even when auto_remediate=low|medium|high, defeating M147 AC-06. Align the review/flow skill vocabulary to low|medium|high and add a contract test that pins the exact accepted labels and forbids the stale blocker/major/minor/nit vocabulary.
findings.author: pi-external-reviewer
findings.summary: auto_remediate cannot classify the severities the review skill tells agents to file
findings.rationale: The feature is agent-enforced, so contradictory skill text is executable behavior, not a documentation nit. Green threshold tests only exercise low/medium/high and miss the actual reviewer instructions.

findings.description: templates/skills/mp-runner/executing.md:24-27 claims the milestone with mp milestone set-status before consulting branch_strategy, contradicting templates/skills/mp-runner/SKILL.md:107-110, which says to branch before claiming. For per-milestone this makes the first plan write occur on the old branch before the switch. The SKILL.md table also says to cut from hard-coded main, which fails in repositories whose default branch is master (including this repository) or another name. Consult and honor branch_strategy before the claim write, create from the current approved base/HEAD unless a repository default is discovered, and pin ordering/portable-base wording in skill_contract_automation tests.
findings.author: pi-external-reviewer
findings.summary: per-milestone branch guidance runs after claim and hard-codes main
findings.rationale: M147 enforcement lives entirely in the skill. Wrong ordering and a non-portable base branch can make the declared branch policy fail or strand the claim mutation on the wrong branch.

findings.description: templates/skills/mp-runner/SKILL.md:89-97 and 124-132 plus templates/skills/mp-runner/executing.md:88-99 instruct git add/commit before mp milestone complete. This contradicts crates/mp/src/config.rs:60-61 and 424-426, which define commit_after_execute as committing after complete, and means the lifecycle/evidence mutations written by complete are left dirty outside the automated commit. It can also create a commit for work that complete subsequently rejects on red AC verification. Run mp milestone complete first; only after it succeeds and lifecycle is confirmed terminal should commit_after_execute=true stage and commit the resulting code plus plan evidence. Add contract tests that assert complete precedes git commit in both runner documents.
findings.author: pi-external-reviewer
findings.summary: commit_after_execute commits before completion instead of after it
findings.rationale: The current sequence violates the knob name and documented hand-off boundary, leaves the audit trail uncommitted, and can commit failed work.
